tool_args.rationale: The five same-horizon rows and the fast-transient/slow-horizon signatures leave a genuine ambiguity between snapshot and temporal-folding mechanisms. The open-branch probe is the least costly relevant measurement.

considered_alternatives.option: author a present-snapshot power-law or second-order model
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Five observations at one horizon do not distinguish the supplied snapshot mechanisms from a temporal folding law; the signatures indicate transient dynamics.
All current rows are already at the target horizon H=3.6, so another long-horizon measurement is less informative than resolving the open mechanism branch.
More costly than the open-branch probe and premature before the mechanism branch is identified.
Auxiliary high-variance measurements do not address the identified model ambiguity.
